key_insight: The paper shows that a structured LLM-guided search can discover new families of quantum LDPC codes by evolving algebraic concepts plus executable code, rather than designing codes from scratch.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical discovery pipeline for scalable quantum error-correcting codes, which are a key bottleneck for building fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
method: Structured concept evolution (SCE) couples a large language model with a mutation grammar.
Concepts combine algebraic specifications with executable programs that instantiate lifted-product CSS qLDPC codes.
Hierarchical mutations explore group algebra, protograph geometry, and base space variants.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports discovery and characterization of diverse competitive code families, evaluated under code-capacity depolarizing noise with BP+OSD decoding.
watch_item: Performance is reported in a limited noise/decoder setting, so real hardware behavior and broader decoding robustness remain to be validated.
paper_title: Large-Language-Model Discovery of Quantum LDPC Codes through Structured Concept Evolution
